key_insight: Coupled Calibration and Learning (CCL) reduces teacher bias in LLM distillation by alternating source-only teacher calibration with target-domain student learning, so the student converges toward the oracle student even without target rewards.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical distillation recipe for shifting domains where target feedback is unavailable, helping smaller models inherit useful behavior without amplifying teacher errors.
method: Calibrate the teacher on source questions using reward feedback only.
Train the student on target questions with the calibrated teacher via token-level branching.
Feed the updated student back into later calibration rounds to progressively reduce bias.
evidence_signal: The paper provides a theoretical guarantee in an autoregressive policy framework: the student's expected average KL divergence to the oracle student converges to zero at a polynomial rate, and it analyzes both calibration error and projected gradient progress.
watch_item: The guarantee is theoretical and depends on iterative calibration quality; in practice, performance may be sensitive to branch design, optimization stability, and how well source rewards reflect target-domain structure.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
